_metadata._susceptibility_note: Edgescan (web app/API = 31.9% of critical+high findings, 2026) and Cobalt (serious-finding prevalence by sector, 2025) measure vulnerability prevalence: whether an attempt would succeed. They belong to the susceptibility assessment, not TEF; using them for TEF multipliers would count exposure twice.

base_rate_triangulation._citation: One population (US organizations): the exfiltration base rate (FBI IC3 data-breach complaints) × the share of breaches through a web application. IRIS sets the floor. TEF = LEF ÷ susceptibility.

base_rate_lef._method: Breaches through a web application: the exfiltration recipe (events, under-reporting, tiers) × the web-app share of breaches. No US count of web-app events exists, so the share carries the scenario.
base_rate_lef._share_note: Judgment, labelled. Inputs: DBIR 2026 Basic Web Application Attacks 10% of breaches (global, all actors); BakerHostetler DSIR 2025 unpatched vulnerability about 25% of network-intrusion root causes (chart read, not web-specific); VCDB US 2013–2022, web application vector in 45% of external hacking or malware incidents with confirmed disclosure (356 / 799). The scenario counts breaches via web applications; defacement, application outages and account-takeover fraud without a breach are not counted (no US count exists).

vector_proportions._citation: DBIR 2026 Web Application pattern, adjusted for exploitation dominance

web_app_overall_share._citation: DBIR 2026 incident classification pattern Basic Web Application Attacks = 10% of breaches (n=22,625 breaches, 2024-2025 data; hand-verified from the PDF). Caveat: DBIR's denominator is breaches, while overall_share is used as a share of all cyber incidents (IRIS basis for ransomware), so the scale is approximate.

web_app_sector_shares._citation: No web-app-specific sector data. All null: the tool uses the IRIS 2025 all-incident sector multiplier (Figure A1) once.

web_app_revenue_shares._citation: No web-app-specific revenue breakdown available. Uses all-incident shares from IRIS 2025.

web_app_revenue_prob_gte2._citation: Not available from IRIS for web-app specifically. All null — tool falls back to overall floor.

credential_tempo._citation: Web-app credential attacks (credential stuffing, brute force). Lower campaign volume than ransomware — attacks are more targeted to specific web applications.

exploitation_scanning._citation: GreyNoise-derived. Web-app exploitation uses a HIGH share of scanning activity — this is the primary vector.
exploitation_scanning.grn_malicious_rate_note: Shared with ransomware: the GreyNoise IP-level malicious rate describes scanning, not the scenario; the scenario enters through ransomware_proportion_of_scanning and PoA.
exploitation_scanning.poa_ransomware_note: Higher PoA than other scenarios — exploitation is the primary success path.
exploitation_scanning.ransomware_proportion_note: Web-app exploitation constitutes a large share of vulnerability scanning.

output_templates.one_sentence: Based on industry data, threat actors {attempt_verb} organizations matching your profile {recurrence} (range: {low} to {high}).
